column3: The Hebrew names his righteousness in a noun phrase; BSB turns it into I am more righteous.
The Hebrew first has a second-person you, then a first-person I; BSB uses first person in both questions.
The Hebrew explicitly names answering with words; BSB says reply.
The Hebrew has no separate word for only; BSB adds only to both clauses.
The Hebrew says He gives songs without explicitly naming us as recipients; BSB adds us.
The Hebrew names emptiness without an explicit word for pleas; BSB supplies pleas.
